newsitem.title: BULGARIA: France's Danone to stay in Bulgaria despite losses.
newsitem.headline: France's Danone to stay in Bulgaria despite losses.

text.p: Danone-Serdika, the Bulgarian subsidiary of France's Danone Group, said on Thursday it was to continue its activity in Bulgaria despite huge losses caused by the problems of the local dairy farming sector.

"The company's 1996 financial results are strongly negative...the year was catastrophic as Bulgaria's dairy farming is dying... but we decided to stay," Michael Spies, General Manager of Danon-Serdica, told a news conference.

He said it was difficult to convince Danone Group to continue its investment in Bulgaria but finally they decided to stay on in a hope for better conditions for the country's dairy farming and improvement of the overall investment climate.
Spies said that dairy farming in Bulgaria was severely troubled by laws governing the purchase price of milk from dairy farmers, the lack of a pricing mechanism and the low quality of raw milk.

Danone-Serdica, set up as a joint venture between the French group and Bulgaria's biggest state-owned milk and yogurt producer Serdika-1 in May 1993, produces Danone yogurt and currently holds 27 percent of the local market, Spies said.
The company had posted a loss of 239.9 million levs last year, its 1996 balance-sheet presented to Reuters showed. Spies said he expected financial results for this year to be negative as well.

After a rise of the capital by $4 million to $15 million in June, Danone Group holds 53 percent of the Danone-Serdica, 33 percent are held by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the 10 percent by the Bulgarian state.
